name: devin-bundle
description: Devin CLI bundle: skills I use + consolidated rules. Cross-platform installer. Unified and adapted engineering + productivity skill sets.

skills.name: project-setup
skills.purpose: Use when starting work on a new or existing project that lacks a `.devin/` configuration, or when the user wants to add skills, hooks, rules, and local tools to a project in a systematic, validated way.

skills.name: ask-matt
skills.purpose: Use when deciding which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo — maps idea-to-ship flows, on-ramps, and standalone tools.

skills.name: autonomous-gates
skills.purpose: Use when running long-horizon or multi-step tasks where quality must be verified before proceeding, when the user asks for "autonomous mode" or "run unattended", or when a task has explicit acceptance criteria that must pass before declaring done.

skills.name: code-review
skills.purpose: Use when completing a task, reviewing a branch or PR, before merging, or when the user asks to 'review since X'.

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.purpose: Use when designing modules, seams, adapters, and the structure of a codebase.

skills.name: context-folding
skills.purpose: Use when context is growing large (approaching model window limits), when long documents or transcripts need to be processed, or when compaction is losing critical information. Adapts Recursive Language Model (RLM) techniques to the Devin CLI runtime.

skills.name: context7
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks about a library, framework, or component and up-to-date docs would help.

skills.name: context-window-hygiene
skills.purpose: Use when a conversation is getting long and the agent seems to be forgetting earlier instructions, before adding MCP servers or rules files, when deciding whether to clear or compact the chat, or when context window budget feels tight. Covers lost-in-the-middle, clear-vs-compact, and lean-context hygiene.

skills.name: debug-ci-failures
skills.purpose: Use when CI is failing and the cause needs to be found across builds, jobs, or environments.

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.purpose: Use when the user says 'diagnose', 'debug this', reports something broken, throwing, failing, or slow, or when encountering a bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior and a fix is not yet obvious.

skills.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
skills.purpose: Use when facing two or more independent tasks with no shared state or ordering.

skills.name: domain-modeling
skills.purpose: Use when building or refining a project's domain model, glossary, or bounded contexts.

skills.name: executing-plans
skills.purpose: Use when executing a written implementation plan with checkpoints and reviews.

skills.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skills.purpose: Use when the implementation is complete, all tests pass, and the work needs to be integrated.

skills.name: gh
skills.purpose: Use when interacting with GitHub via the gh CLI from an agent.

skills.name: git-helper
skills.purpose: Use when managing branches, writing commits, or resolving simple git workflow questions.

skills.name: grilling
skills.purpose: Use when exploring and stress-testing ideas before committing to a design or plan.

skills.name: handoff
skills.purpose: Use when the user needs to compact the current conversation into a document for another agent to continue.

skills.name: implement
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to implement a feature or fix from a spec or set of tickets.

skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to evaluate module depth, identify deepening opportunities in a codebase, and act on them.

skills.name: jira
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks to interact with Jira — search issues, read or update tickets, transition status, add comments, list projects, or run JQL. Routes operations through the Atlassian Rovo MCP server (mcp__atlassian__* tools).

skills.name: mcp-context-audit
skills.purpose: Use when considering adding an MCP server, when context feels bloated with tool definitions, when auditing which MCP servers consume the most context window budget, or before committing a change to mcp_config.json. Estimates per-server tool-definition token cost and flags bloat.

skills.name: mutation-testing
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks to find testing gaps, mutation test, or identify surviving mutants.

skills.name: observability-quality
skills.purpose: Use when adding logging, metrics, distributed tracing, error monitoring, linting, architecture testing, or test infrastructure to a project. Covers OpenTelemetry, Sentry/Datadog/Grafana, Biome/ESLint, ArchUnit, commitlint, Knip, Playwright, and coverage strategy.

skills.name: primeagent-reference
skills.purpose: Use when (1) researching agent harness design patterns, comparing Devin CLI to PrimeAgent/RLM architectures, or evaluating which PrimeAgent features could be adapted to Devin CLI; (2) emulating A2A messaging between subagents or between subagents and the parent agent across time within Devin CLI's ephemeral subagent runtime; (3) capturing recurring failure patterns or reusable tactics as skills/rules/hooks via the Continual Harness /refine self-improvement loop; or (4) deciding whether to dispatch a subagent, which profile to use, and how many concurrent agents to run (subagent dispatch profile/budget selection).

skills.name: project-memory
skills.purpose: Use when the session produces knowledge worth remembering across sessions, such as answered user questions, business rules, project conventions, failed approaches, reusable solutions, or decisions. Captures it with user approval and stores it as plain-text notes inside .devin/ for future retrieval.

skills.name: prototype
skills.purpose: Use when a throwaway prototype is the fastest way to answer a design question.

skills.name: receiving-code-review
skills.purpose: Use when the user receives code review feedback and needs to decide how to act on it.

skills.name: research
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks a question that needs investigation against primary sources and citations.

skills.name: resolving-merge-conflicts
skills.purpose: Use when a merge conflict needs to be resolved and verified.

skills.name: self-extend
skills.purpose: Use when evolving the agent's own capabilities with a new skill, custom subagent, plugin, hook, MCP server, or project rule.

skills.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
skills.purpose: Use when configuring a repo for the engineering skills — set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

skills.name: setup-pre-commit
skills.purpose: Use when setting up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Covers adding pre-commit hooks, configuring Husky, lint-staged, or commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.

skills.name: tdd
skills.purpose: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix and a test-driven approach is appropriate.

skills.name: teach
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to learn a skill or concept through a guided, multi-step session.

skills.name: tool-and-skill-discovery
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks how to do something, needs the right skill or tool, or no skill seems to match the task.

skills.name: triage
skills.purpose: Use when moving issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles — categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

skills.name: using-git-worktrees
skills.purpose: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from the current workspace.

skills.name: using-skills
skills.purpose: Use when starting any conversation and before taking any non-trivial action.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.purpose: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing.

skills.name: wait-what
skills.purpose: Use when the last message did not land and needs to be re-explained or re-pitched.

skills.name: wayfinder
skills.purpose: Use when planning work too large for one session as a map of decision tickets.

skills.name: wizard
skills.purpose: Use when a human must walk through a manual procedure such as provisioning, credentials, or a one-off cutover.

skills.name: writing-for-agents
skills.purpose: Use when creating or editing skills, `.devin/global_rules.md` / `.devin/rules/*.md` rules, or other docs an agent must read.

skills.name: writing-plans
skills.purpose: Use when turning a spec into a concrete, task-by-task implementation plan.

skills.name: writing-skills
skills.purpose: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment.

skills.name: planning-pipeline
skills.purpose: Use when turning conversation into a written spec, breaking a plan or spec into independent traceable tickets, or when a decision cannot be fully answered and needs input from another person via a questionnaire.

skills.name: obsidian-workflow
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to build or update a local codebase wiki in Obsidian, reorganize/refactor an Obsidian vault or docs folder, audit/validate Obsidian project wikis, or compare wiki knowledge across sessions. Four modes: Build, Reorganize, Audit, Cross-session.

skills.name: deep-mode
skills.source: devin-bundle (new, replicates cloud Ask Devin Deep Mode)
skills.purpose: Use when the user says 'deep', 'deep search', 'deep research', or asks for exhaustive codebase exploration beyond a quick grep. Multi-pass agentic search with citations.

skills.name: data-analyst
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks to query a database, analyze data, create charts, or asks business questions about data. SQL-first exploration via MCP data sources.

skills.name: playbook
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to create, refine, or use a reusable playbook for repeated tasks. Structured prompt template with Procedure, Specs, Advice, Forbidden Actions.

skills.name: continuous-improvement
skills.purpose: Use when starting a self-improvement session. Enforces FASE 0 deep research and the 10-step improvement loop so no step is skipped, no phantom failure is invented, and every change is validated with held-out tests.

skills.name: unlazy
skills.purpose: Use when a task is at risk of agent laziness (large, multi-step, previously half-done, or with clear acceptance criteria) to force proof of completion through a gates ledger instead of trusting agent reports.

skills.name: effort-calibration
skills.purpose: Use when choosing a reasoning effort level for an LLM coding agent, when a task seems to be over-thinking or spending too many tokens, when deciding whether to raise effort, when writing task specifications that substitute for reasoning budget, or when a simple task is being treated as a codebase audit. Covers overthinking, compute-optimal test-time scaling, prompt-induced waste, and difficulty-matched effort.

skills.name: mcp-lazy-enablement
skills.purpose: Use when deciding which MCP servers to keep active, when context feels bloated from unused MCP tools, when a task only needs one MCP server temporarily, or when auditing which servers to enable/disable per task. Guides selective MCP enablement to minimize context-window tax.

skills.name: memory-hygiene
skills.purpose: Use when deciding whether to use cross-session agent memory (MEMORY.md, auto-memory), when auto-memory seems stale or bloated, when preferences leak across unrelated tasks, or when choosing between stateless and memory-equipped operation. Covers memory accumulation, temporal contamination, reasoning drift, and user-authored vs auto-saved preferences.

skills.name: impeccable
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks for UI/UX work, wants to fix or polish a page/component, or when an interface looks bland, inconsistent, or like a default template.

skills.name: pr-review
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks to review a Pull Request on GitHub with inline comments and code suggestions via the GitHub API. Enforces a repeatable cycle of check -> comment/suggest -> check next, with a gates ledger for evidence.

skills.name: ai-coding-dictionary
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks about AI coding jargon, wants to clarify a term like context engineering, harness engineering, prompt engineering, or agent harness, or when the agent needs to agree on a term definition before continuing a technical discussion.

skills.name: review-cadence
skills.purpose: Use when deciding how much human review and upfront planning a task needs based on its size, risk, and blast radius, or when the user asks whether a change can skip grilling and go straight to implementation.

skills.name: deploy
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to release, deploy, rollback, or verify a deployment pipeline. Covers CI/CD gates, environment checks, canary/blue-green, and post-deploy smoke tests.

skills.name: security-audit
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to audit code, dependencies, or infrastructure for security issues. Covers SAST, dependency scanning, secret leak detection, and OWASP-style checks.

skills.name: performance
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to profile, optimize, load-test, or measure the performance of code, queries, or infrastructure.

skills.name: a11y-audit
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to check a frontend for accessibility. Covers keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels, color contrast, focus management, and WCAG alignment.

skills.name: api-design
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to design, review, or document an API. Covers REST, OpenAPI, versioning, error models, contract testing, and authentication.

skills.name: database
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to design, migrate, query, or optimize a database. Covers schema design, migrations, query review, indexing, and data integrity.

skills.name: e2e-testing
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to add, run, or debug end-to-end tests. Covers Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, happy paths, critical user journeys, and CI integration.

skills.name: cost-optimization
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to reduce token, compute, or infrastructure costs. Covers context window budget, MCP selection, caching, model routing, and query optimization.

skills.name: docker
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to build, run, compose, or deploy containers. Covers Dockerfiles, docker compose, images, volumes, networks, and basic Kubernetes manifests.

skills.name: i18n
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to add or review internationalization and localization. Covers locale files, translation keys, pluralization, RTL, and date/number formatting.

skills.name: legacy-refactor
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to modernize legacy code incrementally. Covers strangler-fig, seams, characterization tests, safe extraction, and risk reduction.

skills.name: devin-manager
skills.purpose: Use when auditing or managing a project's `.devin/` configuration, producing deterministic read-only reports, detecting broken references, duplicates, and divergences, and generating plans that only persist under `.devin/` after explicit approval.

skills.name: structured-knowledge-extraction
skills.purpose: Use when extracting entities, relations, evidence, and provenance from Markdown or plain text into a typed, versioned knowledge graph under `.devin/`.

skills.name: youtube-fetcher
skills.purpose: Use when you need to turn a YouTube URL and provider-supplied caption/metadata JSON into a raw, timestamped transcript + metadata Markdown note under `.devin/notes/youtube/` for later structured extraction, without auto-installing dependencies, invoking yt-dlp/Whisper, or calling the network.

skills.name: leo
skills.purpose: Use when starting a Devin CLI session in this bundle and the next skill or workflow is not obvious, or when the user needs a quick entry point to seed local AFK issues.

skills.name: afk-loop
skills.purpose: Use when you want the agent to work unattended through local Markdown implementation issues, picking the next ready task from a DAG of blocking relationships.
